https://www.politico.eu/article/gabriel-.text: Former prime minister and presidential candidate Gabriel Attal has filed a complaint over an alleged Russian disinformation campaign ahead of next year’s French presidential election, local news outlets reported on Saturday. Attal’s lawyers told French media that the complaint, filed on Friday, denounces “acts of foreign interference, manipulation of information, fabrication of content likely to undermine the fundamental interests of the nation and the sincerity of the upcoming presidential election.” They told BFMTV that several accounts on social network X, some of which impersonated French and international media, had disseminated fake video reports and newspaper articles attributing false statements to Attal that were “intended to discredit him as a candidate.” Advertisement Advertisement Attal, the candidate of President Emmanuel Macron’s Renaissance party, said earlier this week that he had been a victim of attempted election interference originating in Russia, and that he expected such destabilization efforts to increase ahead of the April 2027 presidential election. Viginum, the country’s agency for fighting online disinformation, confirmed it had detected the operation against Attal and said it bore the hallmarks of pro-Russian disinformation tactics. Attal is the latest French presidential candidate to have fallen victim to such disinformation campaigns. Former prime minister Edouard Philippe was reportedly targeted last week, as was center-left parliamentarian Raphaël Glucksmann .

https://www.planetf1.com/news/fernando-a.text: Fernando Alonso has responded to Aston Martin's new performance level. Fernando Alonso has warned that, despite progress at Aston Martin , there is still “a long way to go” before the team and Honda can count themselves as contenders. An extensive upgrade was brought to Aston Martin’s chassis for the Hungarian Grand Prix, and Wednesday is set to see the debut of an updated power unit from Honda, as the AMR26 takes in a filming day. Fernando Alonso: Aston Martin has ‘long way to go’ despite progress Want more PlanetF1.com coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust . Aston Martin fell behind Cadillac to the back of the F1 pack in recent races, with the team having opted to introduce its first significant round of upgrades in Hungary rather than smaller, incremental improvements, in the hope of a larger step in performance. Alonso got through to Q2 for the first time in 2026 as a result of its early progress, with Honda’s updated engine set to debut at the Dutch Grand Prix after the summer break. While Aston Martin had hoped to hit the ground running in 2026, its improvements at the Hungaroring saw the team seemingly leapfrog Williams, Cadillac, and Haas in the race pecking order. However, there are still further hurdles from here. “We are one team. We work together. We know our weakness and we try to help each other,” Alonso told PlanetF1.com and others in Hungary. “I think Honda was trying to help some of the weaknesses of the car at the beginning of the year. Now with the chassis, we try to help Honda as much as we can, and with also the consistency on laps, on deployment. “I think a lot of help from Aston Martin as well on that regard, on that software department. “It’s a long way to go. We understand that, we are aware of that, but this hopefully is the first step, and both factories are gaining confidence and trust in what they do, so that that probably will be more important than anything else for the next few months.” More about Aston Martin and its new updates All eyes on Aston Martin and Newey as FIA reveals 16-part AMR26 upgrade Honda confirms engine upgrade debut in new Aston Martin boost With a massive 16-part upgrade having gone onto the car, the AMR26 looked distinctly different in Hungary as the Adrian Newey-led design team made significant changes. Newey said there will be more parts to come in future races, and with so much having changed on the car, Alonso hopes to make further inroads into how to make the best of the new package. “I think as expected, more or less the correlation is good and the performance gains are there, what we expected,” Alonso explained. “I think it’s obviously early days with this new car. It’s a completely new car, new concept, so more to come, maybe on setup, optimisation, and things like that. “Next races also with the engine upgrade, it will be an interesting check in Zandvoort [of] where we are and what we can fight for.” Additional reporting by Thomas Maher Want to be the first to know exclusive information from the F1 paddock? https://www.politico.eu/article/french-g.text: PARIS — France will spend more than €1 billion to help its farmers cope with a summer of devastating heat and drought, French Agriculture Minister Annie Genevard said on Friday. The package aims to compensate farmers for their losses, prevent bankruptcies and ensure that agricultural production gets back on track, in particular to enable the purchase of seeds and fodder, the minister said. Between 30,000 and 35,000 farms, or about 10 per cent of French farms, “are in a precarious situation or at risk of becoming so,” Genevard warned. Advertisement Advertisement Three schemes account for the bulk of the government’s spending under the new plan. France will speed up payments under its “national solidarity” scheme designed to compensate for crop losses. It will be topped up to a total of €520 million, provided the country's 2027 budget is duly adopted. An “agricultural recovery fund” of €235 million aims to provide targeted support for the hardest-hit and most vulnerable farms across the produce, cereal and livestock sectors. Finally, a targeted tax relief scheme on unbuilt land will cut €330 million in tax revenue for the state. The government is also considering extending a program helping farmers to purchase fertilizer and non-road agricultural diesel. Genevard also suggested that the retail sector could "play its part" by keeping price rises in check. Part of her plan is already funded for this year, but more cash will need to be allocated in next year's budget, which is set to be presented by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu at the end of September. Advertisement Advertisement “This is new money,” Genevard said. The government is also expected to set out the details of a broader “recovery plan” for farmers, with key measures to be included in the 2027 budget. Lecornu recently promised a tax depreciation scheme for “projects aimed at the future of agriculture,” alongside other measures to “continue adapting agriculture to climate change.”
